The curve gradually rises from about 48° at point E, reaches 90° once on each side around H, is slightly lower than 90° near day H, then declines again, and reaches about 48° again at point F. The figure indicates that M is the midpoint of EH, and N is the midpoint of HF. Then reason: On day H the noon sun in this place is due south, and H lies between the two times of direct solar radiation, indicating that this place is in the tropical region of the Southern Hemisphere. H corresponds to the sun's position near the Tropic of Capricorn around the Southern Hemisphere summer solstice and Northern Hemisphere winter solstice, namely the Northern Hemisphere winter solstice/Southern Hemisphere summer solstice; therefore E and F correspond to adjacent Northern Hemisphere summer solstices, and M is the midpoint from E to H, corresponding to the Northern Hemisphere autumn equinox. Beijing is located in the Northern Hemisphere, and the period when days are longer than nights and the days are getting shorter is from the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice to the autumn equinox. In the figure, the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice to autumn equinox corresponds to E to M, so the answer is EM.
